title: Persistence of divots in missing-difference distributions
statement:
Let $P_n^{\mathrm{H}}(k)$ denote the probability distribution associated with the relevant diffset statistic, and call $k$ a **divot** of this distribution when it is a local depression. Let $n_1$ be a positive integer.

**Divot persistence conjecture.** If $k$ is a divot of $P_{n_1}^{\mathrm{H}}$, then $k$ is also a divot of $P_n^{\mathrm{H}}$ for every $n>n_1$.

This conjecture asserts that once a divot appears, its location never changes as $n$ increases. The source gives no resolution status.
source_name: Scott Harvey-Arnold, Steven J. Miller and Fei Peng, “Distribution of missing differences in diffsets”, arXiv:2001.08931 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08931

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).
